articles.title: Russell Brand, David Walliams and Married at First Sight: Is this a reckoning for TV?
articles.summary: These stories represent the consequences of changes that began years ago, rather than being a sudden cultural shift.
articles.body:
This week, the dark side of television has come crashing into the open.

On Monday, disgraced entertainer Russell Brand was jailed for rape and sexual assault.

Twenty-four hours later, author and comedian David Walliams was unmasked and accused of preying on young women.

By Friday the Metropolitan Police had launched an investigation into further allegations about him.

Also in the last week, Married at First Sight UK has been cancelled following allegations of rape on the hit TV show.

These are all very different stories, but each can be seen as a major reckoning with abuse of power and culture in the industry.

In reality, the glut of recent days is something of a coincidence.

All these revelations began with journalistic investigations that started years ago.

From my own experience - including in my Panorama on Married at First Sight UK - I know investigations typically take a very long time to reach a conclusion, from initial tip-off, to evidence-gathering, corroboration, getting responses, and eventually reporting.

"The truth is, these stories have a long build up. It can be incredibly difficult to get [them] in the papers," Sunday Times columnist Hadley Freeman told me.

In the case of Brand, there was then a police investigation too, before an outcome was reached in court.

Together these stories represent the consequences of changes that began years ago, rather than a sudden cultural shift in the entertainment industry.

It should also be said that Walliams denies the allegations against him . The men accused of rape and sexual misconduct on MAFS UK have also denied all the allegations.

What has changed is that women (because it almost always is women) have seen others speaking up - which, according to broadcaster Kirsty Wark, has given them "courage to do the same". She describes those who have come forward as "beyond brave".

When looking at what’s driving more women to speak up, much can be traced back to the revelations about Harvey Weinstein and the #MeToo movement.

It changed the perception of whether victims would be believed.

In the past, women alleging this sort of behaviour faced barriers - being seen as opportunistic, fearing retaliation, believing they might be the only one.

Now, there can be a snowball effect. Once one, two or three come forward, that prompts others to revisit their experiences - which they may have dismissed or subdued.

"There is more of a sense that you will now be listened to," said Freeman.

It's also clear that when women see action taken, it can encourage others to speak up as well - as it helps counter the widely-held assumption that reporting abuse results in nothing.

When another high-profile man, MasterChef presenter Gregg Wallace, faced accusations of a very different and much lesser order, relating mostly to inappropriate sexual language and humour, the reaction was similar.

Last summer, an independent inquiry upheld dozens of claims against him, and he was sacked . Wallace said "none of the serious allegations" against him had been upheld but that he was "deeply sorry for any distress caused".

One young woman I spoke to in my investigation into Wallace texted me at the time, to give her reaction to his sacking.

"I really believe this will encourage young girls going into the TV industry to have the courage to speak up, if they feel something is wrong," she told me.

But unions say it is still difficult for junior freelance workers, who often find their income unstable and unpredictable, to speak up.

Vulnerable workers "continue to fear raising concerns", said head of broadcast union Bectu, Philippa Childs.

She's echoed by Freeman, who said an "attitude of protecting the talent" remained.

"There will always be wealthy famous predators," she said. But, she added: "Hopefully more and more people at TV stations and movie studios are willing to hear these young people and will take them seriously”.

For more senior people in TV, raising the alarm can also be difficult.

Earlier this week, comedian Lucy Beaumont told Sky News: "The reason high-profile people are not saying anything is because they lose work, because you're seen that you might be a trouble causer. It does need to be said that there needs to be some intervention."

Social media has also played a role in encouraging people to speak up.

And policing investigations have had to keep pace - and adapt - with media scrutiny often prompting authorities to investigate.

Attitudes towards women who speak up are also starting to change – although not always.

Some of what unfolded in court during the Russell Brand case felt like a throwback to how rape cases used to be conducted.

Many have commented on Brand's lawyer's defence tactics against the accusers on the stand - behaviour Freeman said would have been "standard" in the past.

But Freeman noted it was heartening to hear the judge’s remarks in summing up the case - which have also been widely shared by women online and praised for dispelling rape myths.

When Mr Justice Bennathan sentenced Brand to ten-and-a-half years, he told him: "Whatever women wear, wherever they go, indeed whatever they drink, they retain the right to say no."

"I think attitudes have changed,” said Freeman. “It doesn't mean those assaults don't happen any more but attitudes around them have changed.”

Events of the past few weeks highlight how figures who rose to prominence in the nineties and noughties did so in an era with different standards.

Lad culture and celebrity status shielded Brand and others from scrutiny .

Now, behaviour once dismissed as eccentricity or womanising is increasingly being reassessed and called out. Times are catching up with some men of that era.

However, it would be an error to assume this sort of behaviour is confined to the past.

"This is not just about nineties/noughties culture," Wark told me. "It can't be dismissed as a hangover of the past, this is about right now and the industry changes that must happen.

"There will be more cases to come, sexual abuse, coercive control, verbal and physical abuse. It is not OK, and it never was OK."

This week, comedian Deborah Frances-White told BBC Radio 4's The World at One that young women were "definitely" still being exploited in the comedy industry.

And in the past few days, I've had tip-offs about other celebrities allegedly abusing their power. No doubt other journalists have too.

None of those is reportable, yet. As Freeman said: "There are other names out there, but you and I couldn't name them as we'd be sued".

But one "cheering thing", she said, was that the sort of jokes and innuendos from the nineties and noughties, or even the optics of seeing a much older man with a younger girl would no longer be "glossed over".

"It wouldn't be laughed at, and it wouldn't be 'nudge nudge'," Freeman said. "That kind of open, in your face, weirdness won't happen any more".

"On the downside, that may make it harder to identify predators, if it means these things are kept more in the shadows."

Then there’s the use of gagging orders and other legal routes often used by celebrities and media organisations to stop women speaking out.

Last week, a High Court judge rejected an injunction request by Walliams, clearing the way for him to be named.

"There are lots of barriers to speaking out, and those that have access to wealth or fame will often use legal measures to deter alleged victims from doing so," Harriet Wistrich, from the Centre for Women's Justice, told me.

This week, multiple government ministers have spoken against non-disclosure agreements and called for further restrictions on their use.

Next week, Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy will convene industry leaders to urge them to improve safeguarding practices - while Channel 4 bosses are due to appear in front an MPs on Tuesday.

When MAFS UK was cancelled, Channel 4 said the programme had "run its course" and apologised to the women involved in the investigation.

It said the review found that in Channel 4 and production company CPL's handling of the issues raised at the time, there was no breach of Ofcom's broadcasting code.

There is growing recognition that those at the top of media organisations have a responsibility to root out abuse. It can't just be down to the victims.

"People in positions of power have a duty to speak up too," said Wark.

"Broadcasters, production companies and those financing productions all have a responsibility to ensure protections are upheld," added Josephine Brassey, from Women in Film and TV, while Philippa Childs urged the creative industries to accept that their current internal reporting mechanisms were "inadequate".

What everyone seems to agree on is that this can't be another empty tipping point with no real, lasting change.

Maybe this time it could really be a watershed moment.

articles.title: Keaton Slater's parents' fight to bring Latvian killer to UK
articles.summary: How the parents of Keaton Slater, 12, battled to bring the man who killed him to justice.
articles.body:
Days after her 12-year-old son was killed by a BMW driver travelling at 70mph, Louise Slater sat outside the suspect's home, gathering the courage to plead with his family to hand him in.

She had been given the name and address of Aleksanders Dolars after her son Keaton was killed in a hit-and-run in Coventry.

Distraught, she was preparing to knock on the door when a neighbour approached and asked what she was doing.

When she explained, he told her the family, from Latvia, had packed up and left a day or two earlier.

Keaton's suspected killer had fled just hours after leaving him dying in the road.

What followed was a relentless two-year fight by his parents to track him down and bring him back to England to face justice.

He was finally jailed on Friday, for nine years and four months.

Dolars' name had been already circulating locally before police identified him as their main suspect on 18 June 2024, four days after Keaton was killed.

A family waiting at nearby traffic lights said their seven-seater "shook violently" as a BMW driver sped past at what appeared to be far more than the 30mph limit. Moments later, they saw something fly into the air behind them.

As it disappeared from view, the family noticed a black rucksack and a single shoe lying in Radford Road and realised a child may have been hit.

Keaton's father Clint was taken to the scene where he watched as his 12-year-old son's body was covered.

"We just stood there for ages, letting family know what had happened and the whole time I kept thinking, 'he's going to come running up to us in a minute'," she said.

"Then the police came over with a bag and asked, 'is this his'? It was demolished."

Driver who fled to Latvia after killing schoolboy jailed

Killer of boy, 12, ordered to face victim's family at sentencing

Man admits killing schoolboy in hit-and-run crash

In the days after Keaton's death, police reassured Louise airports had been alerted and the suspect would be stopped if he tried to leave the country.

She had been told the family lived on the same road as them and was given a house number.

Summoning the courage to go there, she hoped to appeal to his parents face to face.

"All I was going to say was, 'how can you live with yourselves'?," she said.

"I'd tell them to hold their hands up. Do the right thing. Tell him to face what he's done."

But when she arrived, the family had already gone.

Soon afterwards, people in Latvia contacted her to say Dolars was there. Police later confirmed he had travelled to the country in the weeks after Keaton's death, having tracked him through phone records.

The community quickly rallied around the family and, by August, a petition calling for his extradition had been started.

Yet bringing Dolars back to the UK would prove far from straightforward.

With no extradition treaty in place between the UK and the EU following Brexit, prosecutors and authorities faced a lengthy and complex legal battle requiring co-operation from both countries.

The family intensified their campaign, contacting the Latvian embassy and securing in April 2025 a meeting with Atis Lots, Latvia's ambassador to the UK.

They began by asking whether he was a father. When he said he was, they told him Keaton's story.

Afterwards, they came away convinced they had found an ally.

Bound by confidentiality over much of the discussion, Louise would not reveal details but said the ambassador left them feeling hopeful.

"They wouldn't even call him by his name," she said. "They called him the black sheep of Latvia.

"[They said] 'we don't want him here. We'll do anything we can to get him into your prisons'.

"To walk out of there hearing that, we thought, 'oh my God'."

Taiwo Owatemi, MP for Coventry North West, was working behind the scenes to build political support.

Colleagues in Westminster had warned her that, without an extradition agreement between the UK and EU, securing Dolars' return would be extremely difficult.

However, she was encouraged by the Latvian ambassador telling her his country did not want a difficult relationship with the UK, given the proximity of the country to Ukraine and its continuing war with Russia.

She also learned from him that Latvians were angry at what had happened and that Dolars was bringing shame on their country.

"When you have Latvians in Latvia asking for justice, when you have Latvians in the UK asking for justice, that's his number one job as ambassador," Owatemi said.

Latvians were also proactive identifying where Dolars was in the country, she said.

Louise said she had received messages from families there via a Facebook page set up within the community after Keaton's death.

She said people were saying, "we don't want him here, he's scum".

They also sent a video of Dolars happily walking around and also with his car. She sent them to police.

"He was free. He thought he'd got away with it," she said.

In February 2026, there was a breakthrough.

The Latvian government considered legislation to allow citizens to be extradited to the UK for prosecution.

Campaigning by the family had helped bring about a new law where instances of extradition would now be considered on a case-by-case basis.

"I can't speak for the Latvian government, but for my part I am satisfied that had it not been for their campaigning, had it not been for them keeping Keaton at the forefront of everybody's mind, we wouldn't be where we are today," said Tamina Greaves, specialist prosecutor at the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) in the West Midlands.

She said from the outset there "wasn't an appetite to change the legislation", but the family's "diligence and determination" to articulate the tragedy they were experiencing changed that.

Greaves reviewed the case to decide whether or not there was sufficient evidence to charge Dolars and travelled to The Hague with colleagues to meet Latvian counterparts to try to get him brought back to the UK.

The case is the first time Latvia has extradited an individual since a nationality bar was imposed on the UK in 2021, as part of post-Brexit legislation changes.

Dolars was arrested and detained in Latvia in July this year and extradited a month later.

Det Ch Insp Sam Lewis, from West Midlands Police, said it had been an "indescribable day" for everyone involved in the investigation when he was handed over.

"When you sit down and you look his family in the face, I want to be able to say to them 'we've done everything we possibly can'," she said, adding there were times she could not reveal certain information.

Learning of his extradition through the CPS, Louise said she had burst out crying.

"I said... the first thing I'm going to do is come home and tell Keaton. I talk to Keaton every day," she said.

She said she was incredibly grateful for the help and support and wanted to thank Latvian authorities.

"We had so much love from this... because we weren't community people before this," she said.

"We would just go to work, the boys would go to school, we'd go round to the [social] club every now and then.. so it wasn't like you knew everyone in the street, but now we do.

"It's brought people together as well, not just us with them. It's amazing. What an amazing legacy for Keaton."

articles.title: Even Grand Theft Auto's original creators haven't been able to play GTA 6
articles.summary: The next title in the series is expected to be the biggest video game release ever.
articles.body:
After a 13-year wait, two delays, and several high-profile leaks , the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 is fast approaching.

The next chapter in the nearly 30-year-old series, where players explore open worlds and break the law, has created an extraordinary level of anticipation.

And with developer Rockstar Games keeping their biggest release yet, tightly under wraps, even the people who helped bring the original to life aren't getting special treatment.

"We're all waiting to see what they've done," Dave Jones, GTA's co-creator, tells me, sitting alongside the original game's writer and publicist, Brian Baglow.

Have either of them been able to play the new game ahead of launch?

Baglow shakes his head. He's not complaining, though. "I've got the pre-order," he says.

The original Grand Theft Auto was released in 1997 in Dundee, Scotland by DMA Design, a relatively small team, at least judging by later games' standards.

Following its success with puzzle game Lemmings, the studio was toying around with the idea of making a racing game, initially called Race'n'Chase.

Sitting in the state-of-the-art computer lab at Dundee's Abertay University decades on, Jones tells me the developers still felt they had to bring something new to the table.

"At DMA, we always wanted to do something different," he says. "What was the unique spin we could put on it?"

Part of the answer, he said, came in what feels like a premise gamers take for granted now - "just getting out of the car".

He says the idea of being able to not only drive but switch and steal cars, running about on foot as you did so, meant "all of a sudden you had this interesting mix of gaming coming together".

The team envisioned a game, Jones says, where you could play as both a criminal and a police officer.

But he quickly reconsidered the second option, as it would require players to behave "by the book".

"At some point we just said, you know what, it's way more fun playing the bad guy, so that's what the game was about," he adds.

Despite some of these novel approaches to the game's design, Jones says it was a "slow burn" in sales compared with Lemmings - partly because you had to "play it to get it".

"For the whole of the year that GTA came out, it just kept going and selling and selling," says Baglow.

"And we reckoned it was the word of mouth. The people who had played it going, oh my God, have you played this game?"

Its themes of criminality and violence sparked controversy - leading to debates in the UK Parliament and calls to ban the game. Yet it later transpired much of that was generated by the game's own publisher, BMG Interactive, as a viral marketing stunt.

"We just did things that we felt were fun," says Jones. "We never at any point kind of thought, should we do that? Is it controversial? We never thought that way."

GTA 6 - all you need to know about Rockstar's blockbuster game

Although relatively basic in appearance, with its top-down 2D view and more arcade-like graphics, the original game forged the blueprint for the series' signature satire still seen in much later, more advanced GTAs today.

Despite being set in an exaggerated version of American cities, its Scottishness could still be found in its humour and its outsider perspective, says Guardian video games editor Keza MacDonald.

"It's a deeply satirical game," she says. "It really takes aim at the hyper-individualist, hyper-capitalist nature of the US."

Partly out of necessity due to their comparatively low budget and the cost of real-world licenses, the team came up with cheeky brand names and fake radio stations players could listen to while driving around and causing mayhem.

Though some of these choices were made out of limitations, Baglow says the world-building is the element he's most proud of from the original, which is still a big part of what makes a title feel like GTA.

"It's the business names, it's the radio stations, it's the lyrics, it's the DJs," he says.

"Every part of that is making you believe that this environment you're in is a big cohesive whole."

When GTA V launched in 2013, it made $1bn (£760m) in just three days - faster than any entertainment product had achieved at the time.

The series evolved into a cultural reference point itself - something people recognised, understood and even referenced outside gaming.

"I've seen movies where someone says 'don't go all GTA on me'... it was just surreal," says Jones.

MacDonald, joining me in Glasgow's gaming cafe, RCade, tells me there's an argument now that while earlier GTAs "took a lot" from the big screen, films are now "probably more influenced by GTA" than the other way round.

She says later titles in the series have a cinematic feel, but also reflect the distinct identity it has forged for itself.

As for why Jones believes the game has become such a cultural phenomenon, he says it's the simple fact that it's "based on real life".

"It's not like a lot of games like sci-fi or adventure or fantasy," he says. "There's nothing you have to learn about it, as long as you know a city and driving."

GTA 6 is expected to surpass its predecessor on every level, not only in scale and scope, but also in revenue.

Already, both PlayStation and Xbox, the two platforms the game is initially releasing on, have said the game has become the most pre-ordered title in their digital stores' history.

This may be partly down to its huge size (212GB), meaning many are pre-ordering to "pre-load" the game, ready to play it immediately at launch rather than waiting to download it.

The hype has spilt into the real world, with London's Selfridges transformed into a Vice City-themed pop-up attraction and fictional GTA brands appearing on billboards across Miami, the city that inspired the game.

"Everyone is extremely excited for this," says MacDonald.

"It's hoping to be a shot in the arm for the general games industry, but also every player is looking to see what Rockstar's been doing for all this time.

"It's very rare that we have this one massive game that everybody's going to be, if not playing, then certainly interested in."

Do Jones and Baglow ever wish they were still working on the game now, given the huge amount of global attention focused on it?

"I think everybody loves having their time on it, for one, two, three versions," Jones says.

"But eventually you want to go off and do other things as well."

Baglow adds that watching "the rest of the world fall in love with the game over the last 29 years has just been joyful".

"It means so much to so many people - it's been fantastic."

articles.title: US flight chaos: What caused FAA communication outage that grounded departures nationwide?
articles.summary: A telecommunications outage affecting regional air traffic control centres disrupted air travel across the United States on Friday, prompting the Federal
articles.body: A telecommunications outage affecting regional air traffic control centres disrupted air travel across the United States on Friday, prompting the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to order a nationwide halt to flight departures.What caused the nationwide FAA communication outageThe disruption was caused by overloaded switches and routers in an ageing air traffic control communications system, US transportation secretary Sean Duffy said at a White House briefing.The system became overloaded with data and began transmitting inconsistent information, triggering intermittent communication and radar failures."Our switches, our routers, actually got overloaded with data... They started to give us inconsistency in the data ... and because of that, we shut the system down," Duffy said.According to an airline source cited by CNN, the network router problem spread across the country, affecting communications at multiple air traffic control facilities. The FAA said the ground stop was imposed "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety".The telecommunications failure affected all 22 regional air route traffic control centres responsible for directing aircraft across the US.The disruption raised concerns over air traffic controllers' ability to communicate reliably with pilots, prompting the FAA to suspend departures as a precautionary measure.Also Read| US flight disruptions: Nationwide ground stop ordered for only the second time since 9/11Was FAA outage caused by a cyberattack?US officials said there was no indication so far that the communications failure was the result of a deliberate attack.US President Donald Trump said the disruption was unlikely to have been caused by a cyberattack or artificial intelligence. Homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin also said preliminary assessments did not point to a national security threat."This isn’t the same comparison to 9/11," Mullin told reporters outside the White House, adding that all flights had been accounted for and passengers were safe."There is no indication that we’ve had, no reason to believe, that as of right now this was a threat to the United States," he said.Preliminary reports also indicated that the incident was not a cyberattack, law enforcement sources told CNN. However, authorities continued to examine the cause of the outage and had not ruled out any possibilities.Mullin also dismissed a connection between the FAA disruption and a major Microsoft services outage reported earlier in the week.Also Read| US flight disruption: Air India flags possible delays to US operationsHow many passengers and flights have been affected?More than 4,000 flights were cancelled and over 10,000 delayed across the US following the nationwide ground stop.The disruption grounded flights at airports across the country, leaving an estimated 1.5 million passengers stranded, according to an analysis by data firm Cirium cited by CNN.As flights already in the air continued towards their destinations and landed, the number of aircraft operating across US skies began to decline.With no clear timeline for restoring normal operations, major US airlines were also considering shutting down flight operations for the evening, an airline source told CNN.The impact extended beyond US domestic travel. Air Canada said flights between Canada, the Caribbean and South America that transit US airspace could also be affected by the disruption.Also Read| US flight chaos: Nearly 500 departures disrupted, thousands stranded as FAA halts take-offs nationwide; what we know so farWhat happens next?Transportation secretary Sean Duffy warned that further disruptions to air travel were likely unless the country's ageing air traffic control systems were modernised. He urged Congress to approve legislation providing additional funding to upgrade the infrastructure."You will have more of them unless the American people and the Congress tell us to build, and I can’t wait for that," Duffy said.The FAA and other federal authorities continued working to identify the cause of the telecommunications failure and restore normal operations.However, with no definite timeline for resolution, airlines were preparing for an extended disruption. Passengers were advised to check with their carriers for updates before heading to airports.Trump had been briefed on the situation, while Mullin said the administration was coordinating the response to ensure officials had the necessary resources.The authority later lifted the nationwide ground stop. However, thousands of passengers continued to face travel chaos in what was one of the largest flight disruptions in recent history.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘Planned for 2 months on Instagram’: How girl, 3 friends killed grandpa over money for iPhone, bike in Kottayam
articles.summary: KOTTAYAM: The 13-year-old girl got her friends to murder her 67-year-old maternal grandfather at Karuvatta allegedly to raise money for an iPhone for her
articles.body: KOTTAYAM: The 13-year-old girl got her friends to murder her 67-year-old maternal grandfather at Karuvatta allegedly to raise money for an iPhone for her and a motorcycle for her friend, as per police's chargesheet filed before the juvenile justice board (JJB).The 740-page chargesheet names four juveniles as accused - two of them aged 17, one 16 years and the 13-year-old girl. Police described it a rare case as all four are aged under 18.According to the police, the three boys entered the elderly man's house on Aug 15 night through a ventilation opening after lifting the bathroom roof tile. They allegedly stuffed cloth into the man's mouth and pressed a bedsheet over his face to render him unconscious.They then tied his hands to his thighs with a dhoti and bound his legs with a towel. They then stomped on him and beat him on the neck and head, leading to his death, but no weapons were used, the chargesheet stated. The accused allegedly stole four-and-a-half sovereigns of gold from the house.The crime came to light on Aug 17, and the accused were taken into custody the same day. The investigators said the boys showed the murder scene to the girl over a WhatsApp call. The crime was allegedly planned over two months, with the accused staying in touch through Instagram.All chats were recovered from the accused's phones; information was sought from Meta for verification and the report will be submitted to the JJB, police said.Police recovered six SIM cards from the accused's phones, one of which was active only on the day of the murder, the chargesheet said. The chargesheet cites it as evidence of precise planning. The SIM details were retrieved with help from cyber experts.The case lists 87 witnesses, 98 documents and 12 material objects. Six CCTV clips are cited as key evidence, showing the accused alighting at Haripad railway station, reaching the house and leaving after the act.The prosecution has applied for the three boys to be tried as adults. The JJB will decide after hearing both sides and examining the gravity of the offence, the accused's social background and their mental state. articles.title: Measles-associated deaths reach 10 in US after two more deaths reported
articles.summary: More than 5,400 confirmed measles cases have been recorded in the US to date this year.
articles.body:
Pennsylvania and Wisconsin have announced one additional measles-associated death in each state, marking 10 total deaths in the United States linked to the disease this year.

The Wisconsin Department of Health Services reported an infant’s death on Friday, while the Pennsylvania Department of Health said that its latest death was an unvaccinated patient who had tested positive for measles.

Pennsylvania has logged seven measles-associated deaths, while Wisconsin has reported two. On November 2, New York state said a child had died in the state’s first recorded measles death in more than 30 years.

More than 5,400 confirmed measles cases have been recorded in the US to date, according to data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the Johns Hopkins University International Vaccine Access Center tracker.

The number of confirmed cases as of November 2026 is more than double the 2,289 confirmed cases reported in 2025.

The CDC recorded six measles-related deaths, according to figures on its website. The newly reported data is twice the deaths the agency recorded in 2025.

The CDC’s national death toll is lower than the number of measles-related deaths reported by state officials.

US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr asked CDC director Erica Schwartz not to count the deaths in the official tally, claiming there was no evidence they were measles-associated.

The federal count of measles reports has been at the centre of a dispute between Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro and Kennedy over how measles deaths are classified.

Pennsylvania, the state hardest hit by the outbreak, reports “measles-associated” deaths after a person with confirmed measles dies within 30 days of developing symptoms, unless the death resulted from an unrelated event.

The CDC has said it is working with the Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists to establish a standardised definition for measles deaths.

Infectious disease experts warn that the dispute over how to classify the deaths puts the CDC at odds with a longstanding approach to tracking the consequences of measles.

Epidemiologists have told Al Jazeera that tracking “measles-associated” deaths has long been a standard used by the World Health Organization and the CDC.

Measles, a highly contagious virus, was officially declared eliminated in the US in 2000.

The outbreak comes as vaccination coverage among US kindergarteners has decreased from 95.2 percent during the 2019-2020 school year to 92.4 percent in the 2025-2026 school year.

Local and state health departments have ramped up vaccination efforts.

Measles is preventable through the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine, which offers approximately 97 percent protection after two doses.

As of Friday, Pennsylvania’s Department of Health has logged 1,542 confirmed cases this year, while Wisconsin recorded 651 cases.

As a result of the ongoing outbreak, the US could lose its measles elimination status this week. Elimination status requires that the country in question is able to squash instances of measles transmission for 12 months or more.

articles.title: 85+ Happy Children's Day Messages, Greetings, Wishes and Quotes for 2026
articles.summary: Ask a grown-up what they remember about Children’s Day at school, and the answer is rarely about speeches. It is usually something smaller.
articles.body: Ask a grown-up what they remember about Children’s Day at school, and the answer is rarely about speeches. It is usually something smaller. A sweet handed out by a teacher who never smiled during class. A free period that felt like a gift. A song sung off-key, loudly, with no one minding.In 2026, Children’s Day in India falls on Saturday, 14 November. Many schools hold their events a little earlier, so the celebrations may already be in full swing. Below is the story behind the day, a look at what it asks of adults, and a stack of messages, greetings, wishes and quotes that can be passed along to a child, or to the child still living inside a grown-up.The man behind the day: Who was Chacha Nehru?Jawaharlal Nehru was born on 14 November 1889 in Allahabad, now Prayagraj. He went on to become the first Prime Minister of independent India and held the post from 1947 until his death in 1964. Politics was only part of his public image, though. Children called him “Chacha Nehru”, or Uncle Nehru, and the nickname stuck for decades.One reason the affection felt real is a book. In 1928, while his daughter Indira was a girl, Nehru wrote her a series of letters from Mussoorie, explaining in plain words how the world began, how life took shape and how people came to live in societies. They were later published as Letters from a Father to His Daughter. The letters do not talk down to a child. They assume a ten-year-old can handle big ideas if someone bothers to explain them kindly.That habit of taking children seriously is what people remember. Photographs of him with schoolchildren, often with a rose pinned to his jacket, became part of how India pictured him. He believed that the way a country raises its young decides what the country becomes. He is widely quoted as saying that the children of today will make the India of tomorrow.30 Children’s Day messagesToday belongs to you. The grown-ups are only here to clap, cook and carry your bag.You may be small, but the questions you ask often make the biggest minds stop and think. Never stop asking.Happy Children’s Day! Stay curious, stay kind and stay a little bit naughty.A house without a child’s laughter is just a building. Thank you for making ours a home.Some day you will be grown up and busy. Until then, may nobody rush you.Every scribble on the wall, every mismatched sock, every endless “why?” is a memory in the making. Happy Children’s Day.Wishing you a day with no homework, no hurry and plenty of dessert.The world needs your imagination more than it needs another adult. Keep it safe.You taught us that puddles are for jumping in. We are still learning.May your dreams be loud, your friendships be loyal and your bedtime stories be long.On Chacha Nehru’s birthday, here is a promise: your ideas will always get a seat at the table.Childhood passes quickly, so today, let there be extra games, extra hugs and extra time.You do not have to be perfect. You only have to be you, and that is more than enough.Happy Children’s Day to a little person who makes big days out of ordinary ones.Run, fall, get up, laugh and repeat. That is the whole secret, really.Thank you for reminding every grown-up in this house how to enjoy small things.May you always find the courage to say “I don’t know” and the joy of finding out.Today the rule is simple: whoever is smallest gets to choose the plan.Your smile has fixed more bad days than any medicine ever could.Wishing every child a school that feels safe, a teacher who feels kind and a world that feels fair.Grow at your own speed. Flowers do not compete, and neither should you.If childhood had a sound, it would be your giggle at 7 a.m. on a holiday.Never let anyone tell you your dream is too big. Even the tallest tree began as a seed.To every child who is brave enough to be different: the world is lucky to have you.Today, may every drawing be displayed on the fridge and every question be answered patiently.Happy Children’s Day to the kids we were and the kids we are raising.Eat the ice cream, read the extra chapter, stay up five more minutes. Today allows it.You are not just our future. You are our present, and a very lovely one.May you always have someone to tuck you in and something to look forward to.From all of us who once sat where you sit: enjoy it. It is worth every minute.Wishing every child a world where dreams are encouraged and happiness has no limits.May your days be filled with colourful memories, exciting adventures and countless reasons to laugh.Happy Children's Day! Never let the little spark of curiosity inside you fade away.May you grow with confidence, kindness and the courage to chase everything your heart desires.1. Every child deserves a childhood filled with love, safety and opportunities. Happy Children's Day!20 Children’s Day greetingsHappy Children’s Day to the brightest little stars in our lives!Warm greetings on Children’s Day to every child who makes the world softer.Wishing you a joyful Children’s Day filled with laughter and sweet surprises.Happy Children’s Day to our young dreamers and doers.Sending hugs and happiness your way this Children’s Day.Greetings to the future scientists, artists, teachers and storytellers. Your day has arrived.Happy Chacha Nehru Jayanti and Children’s Day to all the little ones.May this Children’s Day be as colourful as your crayon box.Cheers to a day built entirely of play, snacks and giggles.Happy Children’s Day to the kids who keep the whole family young.Wishing every child a day full of love, light and zero worries.Happy Children’s Day to students, siblings, cousins and neighbours’ kids too.Greetings from a grateful grown-up to a child who teaches more than any textbook.Today is your day. Go be wonderfully, wildly yourself.Wishing you happiness that lasts well beyond the last slice of cake.Happy Children’s Day to little hearts with big hopes.Celebrate today like only a child can: completely and without checking the clock.Warmest wishes on Children’s Day to the ones who make ordinary Saturdays special.May your day sparkle with kindness, curiosity and fun.Happy Children’s Day from everyone who loves you more than they can say.20 Children’s Day wishesMay you always be curious enough to look up at the sky and wonder.May your school bag stay light and your lunchbox stay full.May every teacher you meet believe in you.May you never be afraid to ask for help.May you grow strong without ever growing hard.May your friends be honest and your bedtime be peaceful.May you discover what you love early and keep it forever.May the world be gentle with your mistakes.May you always have a book to get lost in.May your laughter stay louder than your worries.May you learn that kindness is a quiet kind of strength.May you have a lap to climb into on bad days.May you be brave when it matters and silly when it does not.May you play outside more than you scroll inside.May every question you ask meet an honest answer.May you respect others and still respect yourself.May you find joy in simple things, like rain, rhymes and rangoli.May you never feel unseen.May your future be as big as your imagination.May you remember, long after you are grown, how it felt to be this happy today.Keep dreaming big and smiling brighter. Happy Children's DayMay your world always be colourful, magical and full of joy.Stay curious, stay fearless and keep shining like a star!Wishing you endless giggles, beautiful memories and sweet adventures.May happiness follow you wherever your little feet take you.5 Quotes to remember“The children of today will make the India of tomorrow. articles.title: 'She thought he was joking': Gujarat man strangles daughter over inter-caste relationship on Diwali; how it unfolded
articles.summary: VADODARA: A Diwali celebration with the family, a confrontation over her relationship with a man from another caste, and a remark she dismissed as a joke
articles.body: VADODARA: A Diwali celebration with the family, a confrontation over her relationship with a man from another caste, and a remark she dismissed as a joke — a 50-year-old man allegedly strangled his 21-year-old daughter with her dupatta hours after warning that he could kill her, police said.Kaushal Patel allegedly murdered his daughter Saniya around 3.15am on Monday at their home in Metpur village of Anand district, after she refused to end her year-long relationship with a village youth. He then allegedly tried to pass off the murder as suicide, taking her body to a hospital and claiming she had died by suicide.Khambhat Town police registered an FIR against Kaushal and arrested him on Monday. He was produced before a court on Tuesday, where police sought his custody for further investigation. The court rejected the application and remanded him to judicial custody.Police said the family had celebrated Diwali together on Sunday evening before retiring to their rooms late at night. Around 3.15am, while the other family members, including Kaushal's elderly parents, were asleep, he allegedly confronted Saniya in the kitchen over her relationship.Kaushal had repeatedly objected to the relationship because the youth belonged to another caste. He also considered the man's monthly income of Rs 10,000 to Rs 15,000 inadequate, investigators said. Despite repeated pressure from her father to break up, Saniya continued speaking to the youth over the phone.During the confrontation, Kaushal allegedly told his daughter that he could strangle her. Saniya initially dismissed the remark as a joke, police said. He then allegedly grabbed her dupatta and used it to strangulate her, maintaining pressure until she collapsed on the floor.Family claimed she died by suicideAfter the killing, Kaushal and other family members allegedly attempted to make it appear that Saniya had died by suicide. They took her body to Khambhat General Hospital around 5am, claiming she had killed herself.However, doctors found the circumstances suspicious and recommended a forensic postmortem. Her body was subsequently sent to Shree Krishna Hospital in Karamsad for examination.The postmortem established that Saniya had died of ligature strangulation caused by compression of the neck. This prompted police to investigate the circumstances surrounding her death and question family members.During questioning, Kaushal allegedly broke down and confessed to the crime. Police also recovered the dupatta suspected to have been used in the murder and other evidence."There was discord between them over her relationship with a man from the village," said inspector P J Bantva of Khambhat Town police station.Saniya had completed her BCom from Vadodara and was pursuing further studies, police said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Surat | Silver Rate in Surat | Bank Holidays in Surat | Public Holidays in Surat | Surat AQI | Weather in Surat | Petrol Price in Surat | Diesel Price in Surat | CNG Price in Surat | LPG Price in SuratStay updated with the latest Surat news. articles.body: Suspected unauthorised drone activity at a US military airbase in eastern England triggered a security response, raising fresh concerns over the safety of American military installations in Britain. The situation at Royal Air Force (RAF) Lakenheath has since been brought under control, with no damage reported to personnel, aircraft or infrastructure, US and British defence officials said on Friday.Security personnel at the base responded to reports of suspected drone activity, the US Air Forces in Europe said in a statement, according to the Associated Press (AP)."We continue to work closely with our host nation counterparts to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, US and host nation civilians, contractors, and all of our families," the statement said.A spokesperson for Britain's Ministry of Defence confirmed that the situation had been "resolved". The spokesperson said US Air Force security teams had responded to the reports and British authorities were coordinating with their American counterparts to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.The official spoke anonymously because of the sensitive nature of the security matter.The latest incident is the third security-related development involving US military installations in Britain in recent weeks, amid concerns over potential threats to American military assets stationed in the country.US relocates aircraft from RAF Mildenhall after security threatThe incident at RAF Lakenheath comes days after the US relocated more than a dozen aircraft from RAF Mildenhall, another American-operated military base located nearby in eastern England, following a security threat.During the movement of aircraft, RAF Mildenhall raised its force protection condition (FPCON) to Charlie, the second-highest security alert level. The designation is used when an incident occurs or intelligence indicates that a terrorist attack targeting military personnel or facilities may be imminent.A US official had described the relocation as a precautionary measure and not a response to an active attack.Earlier security concerns at RAF FairfordSeveral weeks earlier, British authorities detained a group of men after three suspicious vans were reportedly spotted heading towards RAF Fairford, located around 240 kilometres west of RAF Mildenhall and RAF Lakenheath.British investigators linked the suspected plot to Iran, prompting the US to withdraw bombers stationed at the facility.RAF Fairford, a British-owned military installation, has served as an operating base for American bombers during several decades of military operations in the Middle East, including the Iran war.Further arrests were subsequently made, with at least three men facing charges over an alleged plot to target the airbase.Separately, a US Army officer assigned to a Nato unit at a military installation near Gloucester, England, was arrested this week on suspicion of spying for Russia.Police clarified that the arrest was unrelated to other ongoing counterterrorism investigations, indicating that there was no established link between the case and the suspected Iran-related plot involving RAF Fairford.The developments have brought renewed attention to security arrangements at US military installations across Britain, which play an important role in American military operations and Nato activities.You use AI every day. articles.title: ICC stops probe into alleged crimes by US troops in Afghanistan
articles.summary: The decision follows feuds between the United States and the Hague-based International Criminal Court.
articles.body:
Judges at the International Criminal Court (ICC) have issued a decision to halt the prosecutor’s investigations into alleged crimes by American troops in Afghanistan and instead to focus on the Taliban’s actions since 2021, according to court documents released on Friday.

The ICC’s ruling, which was issued Thursday but only made public on Friday, cites “significant limitations to the Prosecution’s ability to conduct its investigations and secure evidence”.

The decision follows feuds between the United States and the Hague-based ICC, notably after Washington sanctioned 13 current and former ICC staff members over the investigation into alleged crimes by US personnel and arrest warrants issued against Israeli officials.

It closes not only the line of inquiry into alleged crimes by US troops, which had lain dormant since 2021, but also the probe into the ISIL affiliate in Khorasan Province (ISKP).

The prosecutor’s office told The Associated Press and Reuters news agencies that it has already appealed the decision.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio previously said, “President Trump will never allow the International Criminal Court to prosecute Americans.”

In the October statement, Rubio also warned that “the United States will continue its campaign to dismantle the ICC, brick by brick, until Americans are threatened no longer.”

It is not clear if the court’s decision to stop the investigation will affect Washington’s stance on the ICC.

Regardless, the US is not a member of the court and does not recognise its jurisdiction.

The court’s founding statute says that it can prosecute anyone accused of atrocity crimes committed on the territory of ICC member states.

The ICC issued four arrest warrants for Taliban leaders last year.

The investigation in Afghanistan began in 2020, covering offences allegedly committed by Afghan government forces, the Taliban, American troops and US foreign intelligence operatives dating back to 2002.

In 2021, Karim Khan, the probe’s prosecutor, announced he would “deprioritise” the investigation into American forces, citing challenges in obtaining evidence.

Khan was ousted from the court over sexual misconduct allegations earlier this year.

articles.title: In 1985, Willie Nelson joined two musicians to launch Farm Aid as US family farms struggled; 41 years later, the annual concerts and wider campaign have raised over $90 million to support farmers and rural communities
articles.summary: In 1985, Willie Nelson joined fellow musicians Neil Young and John Mellencamp to launch Farm Aid at a moment when family farms across the United States
articles.body: In 1985, Willie Nelson joined fellow musicians Neil Young and John Mellencamp to launch Farm Aid at a moment when family farms across the United States were under severe financial pressure. Four decades later, the annual concert has become one of the country’s most recognisable examples of musicians turning a stage into a platform for social change. According to Farm Aid, the organisation has raised more than $90 million since 1985 to support programs that help farmers thrive, expand access to food from family farms, and challenge the dominance of industrial agriculture.The 2026 festival showed that the mission remains far more than nostalgia. Held in Virginia Beach, the event brought together 14,000 attendees from every US state, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, five Canadian provinces and 19 countries. It also reached millions more through television and online broadcasts, with Farm Aid reporting 8.05 million CNN viewers and more than 3.1 million people watching its YouTube livestream.How Farm Aid beganFarm Aid was created in response to the farm crisis of the 1980s, when falling prices, rising debt and broader economic upheaval left many family farmers struggling to hold on to their land. Nelson, Young and Mellencamp organised the first concert to raise money and public attention for farmers whose livelihoods were being threatened.From the beginning, the idea was not simply to write cheques. Farm Aid positioned itself as an advocate for family-scale agriculture, arguing that the people who grow food should have a viable place in the American economy. The organisation’s stated work includes helping farmers thrive, expanding the reach of what it calls the Good Food Movement, and promoting food from family farms.That combination of music, fundraising and advocacy has proved durable. More than 40 years after the first show, Farm Aid continues to stage an annual festival and to use the attention around it to connect consumers, policymakers and farmers.The musicians behind the missionWillie Nelson, Neil Young, John Mellencamp, Dave Matthews, Margo Price and Nathaniel Rateliff serve as Farm Aid artists and board members, hosting the annual festival. Their involvement has helped keep the cause visible across generations of music fans, while the artists themselves donate their performances each year.The 2026 event featured 18 artists who performed without payment in support of family farmers. That model remains central to Farm Aid’s identity: the concert is not merely a benefit show with famous names attached, but a recurring gathering of performers who lend their time and cultural influence to a long-running campaign.The festival also creates space for farmers to speak for themselves. Before the music began, seven Virginia farmers joined artists on stage for a press event, sharing their experiences and visions for agriculture. Five farmers were also heard on the FarmYard stage, where they discussed pressing issues and shared stories about food and farming in their region and across the country.What the 2026 concert achievedThe 2026 festival was attended by 14,000 people, but its reach extended well beyond the venue. Farm Aid reported 8.05 million viewers across CNN’s global platforms, more than 3.1 million YouTube livestream viewers, and 194 virtual watch parties across 31 states.The event generated 3,300 news stories, with coverage from outlets including Billboard and Rolling Stone. That attention matters because Farm Aid’s work depends not only on donations but on keeping the pressures facing family farmers in the public conversation.The festival also had a local impact. With help from Support+Feed, attendees donated 10,000 pounds of nonperishable food to the Foodbank of Southeastern Virginia and the Eastern Shore. Volunteers from 33 states helped run the event, while 426 farmers and advocates took part in pre-festival events, trainings and farm tours.Food, farming and communityFarm Aid’s 2026 festival made a deliberate effort to connect concertgoers with the people and products behind their food. Its HOMEGROWN Concessions program featured 71 items sourced from local farms, co-ops, food hubs and small businesses, including Virginia peanuts, Chesapeake poutine with hand-picked blue crab, and local cheeses.Six Virginia farmers supplied thousands of flowers, hundreds of corn shocks, pumpkins, gourds and hay bales for the venue’s decorations, along with a tractor. The HOMEGROWN Youthmarket gave young people from FFA, 4-H and Petersburg Is Growing the chance to share fresh produce and baked goods while explaining their work in local communities.There were also 45 HOMEGROWN Village exhibitors, offering hands-on activities about soil, water, energy and food. Demonstrations covered restoring soil with cover crops, making salsa, processing wool and growing mushrooms at home, while a seed swap gave attendees a practical way to participate in the ideas being discussed.More than a concertFarm Aid describes its mission as broader than raising money for individual farmers. The organisation says its work aims to expand the reach of the Good Food Movement, take action to change the dominant system of industrial agriculture, and promote food from family farms.The 2026 event reflected that wider ambition. Twelve policymakers from Virginia spoke with farmers, learned about their challenges and discussed ways to support family farm agriculture. The festival also brought together artists, farmers and advocates for conversations about land, family and legacy, rather than treating farmers only as beneficiaries of charity.Even the environmental details carried the message. Working with Tidewater Compost, Farm Aid diverted more than 12,000 pounds of organic material from landfills to support future crops in Virginia.A legacy still growingMore than 41 years after Willie Nelson, Neil Young and John Mellencamp launched Farm Aid, the organisation has raised more than $90 million. The figure represents decades of concerts, donated performances, volunteer labour and public support for a cause that began during a national farm crisis.The 2026 numbers suggest that the model still resonates. Thousands attended in person, millions watched remotely, and the festival generated both money and attention for family farmers.Farm Aid’s lasting achievement may be less about any single dollar amount than about its persistence. What began in 1985 as an urgent response to farmers in trouble has become an annual institution that continues to connect music fans with the people who grow the country’s food.You use AI every day. articles.title: After hundreds of complaints about smells resembling rotten eggs, sewage and decaying meat, a Chicago judge orders an animal-feed plant to halt odour-causing operations until January 2027
articles.summary: Hundreds of complaints about foul smells from an animal-feed processing facility on Chicago’s Southeast Side have resulted in a court order temporarily
articles.body: Hundreds of complaints about foul smells from an animal-feed processing facility on Chicago’s Southeast Side have resulted in a court order temporarily stopping its odour-causing operations. A Cook County Circuit Court judge issued the order on October 14, 2026, following legal action by Illinois Attorney General Kwame Raoul and the city of Chicago against Pullman Innovations. Residents have reported smells resembling rotten eggs, sewage, garbage and decaying meat, describing disruptions to everyday activities and gatherings. The order gives the company until January 2027 to address the odour problems or bring its operations into compliance with environmental laws.Chicago animal-feed plant faces shutdown over persistent odoursAccording to the Illinois Attorney General’s October 14 announcement, the court granted a temporary restraining order stopping odour-causing activities at Pullman Innovations until January 14, 2027, when the next hearing in the case is scheduled. The restriction could end earlier if the company resolves the excessive odours and complies with environmental requirements before that date.Pullman Innovations is operated by A-F Acquisition LLC and processes a by-product of commercial edible oil into animal-feed ingredients. The Illinois Environmental Protection Agency identifies the facility at 2701 East 100th Street in Chicago, where operations have continued for approximately a decade.The Illinois EPA explains that the site was previously operated by Agri-Fine Inc. before A-F Acquisition LLC acquired it in 2016 following the former operator’s bankruptcy.The facility has been subject to environmental oversight because its operations involve equipment and processes capable of releasing air pollutants. The state agency has received odour complaints dating back to the period when Agri-Fine operated the site.What prompted the legal action against Pullman InnovationsThe legal dispute developed after residents repeatedly reported unpleasant smells affecting their neighbourhood. The Illinois EPA states that hundreds of complaints were documented in the lawsuit, with residents describing frequent odours resembling rotten eggs, garbage, sewage, chemical smells and rotting meat.The August 2026 lawsuit was brought by Attorney General Kwame Raoul, Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson and the city of Chicago against A-F Acquisition LLC. As outlined in the Attorney General’s announcement, the complaint alleged excessive odours, unlawful air pollution, the construction of a boiler without a required permit and violations of conditions attached to the facility’s operating permit.According to the Attorney General’s office, Chicago inspectors encountered odours that made breathing difficult and caused nausea during inspections conducted in response to complaints. Illinois EPA inspectors also recorded strong smells inside and outside the facility during a February 2025 inspection. In August 2026, another state inspection found overpowering odours in nearby residential areas.How have the smells affected the surrounding communityThe impact of the facility's operations has extended beyond occasional discomfort. Residents living nearby have told authorities that the smells regularly interfere with their ability to use their homes and enjoy outdoor spaces.The Illinois Attorney General's announcement describes people being forced to keep their windows shut because of the nauseating odours. Some residents have reportedly been driven indoors while attempting to enjoy outdoor activities, with the smells interrupting family gatherings and other occasions.The effects have also reached community institutions. According to the Attorney General, nearby schools and a local church have experienced problems linked to the odours. Church members have reported that weddings, funerals and outdoor festivals were sometimes disrupted or ruined by the unpleasant smells.Residents have played an important role in documenting the problem. The Attorney General's office said community members tracked and recorded odour incidents, provided sworn statements and kept both the office and Illinois EPA informed about conditions around the plant.The Illinois EPA's website encourages residents dealing with persistent odours to maintain incident logs, explaining that these records can support its ongoing enforcement work.Environmental violations have drawn years of scrutinyThe court order follows several years of regulatory action involving the facility. The Illinois EPA records show that the US Environmental Protection Agency issued Pullman Innovations a notice of violation on March 3, 2022, citing alleged breaches of federal clean-air requirements and Illinois' air pollution rules.In January 2025, Illinois EPA rejected the company's application to construct a third natural gas boiler. The agency explained that the boiler had already been installed before the company applied for the required construction permit.A violation notice followed on May 29, 2025. It alleged that Pullman had installed the boiler without permission, allowed odorous emissions, failed to control smells properly, inadequately maintained existing pollution-control equipment and failed to submit required reports about deviations from permit conditions.The agency subsequently referred the violations to the Attorney General's office for enforcement.Other concerns emerged regarding wastewater. The Illinois EPA reported that community members believed smells might also be connected to wastewater discharged into the sewer system. Following an inspection in April 2026, the agency issued another violation notice in May over concerns involving the facility's wastewater pretreatment system.These actions formed part of the wider regulatory background to the lawsuit and the temporary shutdown order.What changes could be required before operations resumeThe court order is intended to provide relief while the legal proceedings continue and the company works towards addressing the problems. The Attorney General's request for a preliminary injunction outlines several measures that could be required to bring the facility into compliance.According to the Illinois Attorney General's announcement, the proposed requirements include submitting a remediation plan to the Illinois EPA for approval and implementing it within an established timeline. The plan would be expected to identify and address the sources of excessive odours and prevent further environmental violations.The motion also seeks an order requiring Pullman Innovations to complete the installation and begin operating a pollution-control device known as a regenerative thermal oxidiser within 120 days. The equipment is intended to reduce emissions of volatile organic material, which can contribute to the facility's odour problems.The Illinois EPA explains that the company applied to install the device in December 2025 and received a construction permit on June 1, 2026. The application was connected to enforcement efforts over pollution and was not intended to increase the amount of air pollutants the facility is authorised to emit.The temporary restraining order marks a significant development in a dispute that has involved residents, environmental regulators and local government for years.The next hearing, scheduled for January 14, 2027, will consider the Attorney General and city's request for a preliminary injunction requiring the company to address its odour problems and alleged environmental violations.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump, Putin and Xi to hold unprecedented trilateral meet: What's on agenda?
articles.summary: US president Donald Trump plans to discuss global nuclear disarmament with Russian president Vladimir Putin and Chinese president Xi Jinping during an
articles.body: US president Donald Trump plans to discuss global nuclear disarmament with Russian president Vladimir Putin and Chinese president Xi Jinping during an unprecedented trilateral meeting in China next week, the White House said on Friday.Trump will raise the issue of reducing nuclear arsenals during the meeting scheduled for Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-pacific economic cooperation (APEC) forum in Shenzhen, white ouse spokesperson Olivia Wales told reporters."He will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world, whose proliferation president Trump believes is very dangerous," Wales said.Trump's push to make nuclear arms reduction a key agenda item at the first-ever meeting involving the three leaders has reportedly caused unease in Beijing. China is hosting a summit primarily focused on trade and economic cooperation and has repeatedly resisted US efforts to initiate discussions on nuclear disarmament.Washington and Moscow possess the world's two largest nuclear arsenals, while China's stockpile has also been expanding. Beijing has traditionally maintained that nuclear negotiations should primarily involve Russia and the United States because of the significant difference in their respective weapons inventories.A senior Trump administration official acknowledged that the meeting was unlikely to produce an immediate agreement on nuclear arms reduction."We do not expect to get to any kind of agreement," the official said, describing the issue as a difficult one for Beijing to address.However, the official urged China to take a more active role in discussions on global nuclear security, adding that the meeting could mark the beginning of a constructive dialogue."This is the beginning of hopefully a conversation that can be productive going forward," the official said.According to the Stockholm International peace research institute, Russia has the world's largest stockpile of stored nuclear warheads, followed by the United States and China. The new strategic arms reduction treaty (New START), which governed nuclear arms control between Washington and Moscow, expired this year.It remains uncertain whether Putin and Xi will agree to engage in discussions on nuclear weapons reductions with Trump. The Chinese and Russian embassies in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment.Iran war likely to feature in discussionsApart from nuclear disarmament, Trump is also expected to discuss the US-Israeli war against Iran with the two leaders. However, the Russia-Ukraine conflict is unlikely to be part of the agenda, the senior administration official said.Trump is not expected to hold separate bilateral talks with Putin during the visit. He is also unlikely to discuss Ukraine's access to satellite communications services provided by Elon Musk's SpaceX.Musk will accompany Trump on his China visit but will not participate in the trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin, according to the official.Explaining why the Ukraine conflict would not feature in the discussions, the official said Washington had recently held several meetings with Moscow, while Beijing was not directly involved in that diplomatic process."We've had many meetings recently with the Russians, but China is not really a part of that track, so it doesn't seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there," the official said.No meeting planned with North Korea's Kim Jong UnTrump is also not expected to meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his upcoming Asian tour, the administration official confirmed.The US president is scheduled to leave on Monday for a four-day regional visit, which will include stops in China and the Philippines. The planned trilateral engagement with Putin and Xi is expected to put nuclear weapons proliferation and international security at the centre of discussions.You use AI every day. articles.title: Elon Musk and over 40,000 others, including Nvidia’s current and former employees, sign open letter for Jensen Huang’s return; letter says: Thirty-three years of leadership do not place anyone above...
articles.summary: Elon Musk has joined a growing campaign to bring Jensen Huang back as Nvidia CEO.
articles.body: Elon Musk has joined a growing campaign to bring Jensen Huang back as Nvidia CEO. “A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too,” Musk posted on X. He is now one of more than 43,000 people who have signed an open letter to Nvidia’s board, two days after Huang resigned from the company he co-founded 33 years ago.The letter is hosted on a volunteer-run site called Stand with Jensen, and asks the board to reinstate Huang while an independent investigation establishes the facts. Its live counter, which refreshes every 30 seconds, lists 2,980 signers as current Nvidia employees, 454 as former employees and 24,097 as shareholders. The other 15,517 signed as supporters. The campaign says it isn’t endorsed by Nvidia or Huang, and that affiliations are self-reported and unverified.What the open letter to Nvidia’s board demandsThe letter opens with gratitude and turns to process. Signers say they are concerned Huang was removed “without meaningful due process,” and that they haven’t been shown evidence that the woman at the centre of the controversy was a spy. “Suspicion or association alone is not a sufficient basis for ending Jensen’s leadership,” it reads.It makes three demands. The first is to reinstate Huang as CEO, or give a specific, evidence-based reason why his absence serves Nvidia. The second is an independent investigation with a disclosed scope and timeline, and a fair chance for Huang to respond before any final decision. The third is a timely public explanation of the board’s concerns, its evidence and how it weighed the interests of employees and shareholders.The letter stops short of calling Huang blameless. “Thirty-three years of leadership do not place anyone above accountability. But accountability requires evidence, a fair hearing, and a reasoned decision,” it says. “Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice.”Tim Sweeney, Garry Tan and 4,000 Nvidia employees among signersMusk isn’t the only big name. Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Y Combinator’s Garry Tan, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Cohere’s Aidan Gomez and investor Gavin Baker of Atreides Management have signed too. Binance co-founder Yi He left a one-line message: “I wear a leather jacket. I disagree.”Messages from Nvidia staff are more measured. Erwin Coumans, who lists himself as a senior distinguished engineer, wrote that Huang’s private affairs are “none of my business” and that any breach of the code of conduct “has to be dealt with,” but asked for fair treatment. Solutions architect Elias Seyoum pointed to Huang’s own management philosophy. “Jensen talks about not firing for mistakes but using it as an opportunity to learn. Let’s give him that same courtesy,” he wrote.The site also filters what goes up. New signatures may be held for organiser review, and a message showing mockery or negative sentiment toward Huang can get the whole signature rejected.The letter adds to pressure that has been building inside Nvidia all week. An internal suggestion box post urging the board to weigh employee sentiment has drawn more than 1,600 comments, most of them backing Huang’s return, Wired reported. The publication also couldn’t find a single post from an Nvidia employee supporting his exit.Why Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEOHuang stepped down as president, CEO and board member on November 12, effective immediately. Four days earlier, he had admitted in a memo to employees that he was “unfaithful to my wife,” after reports of a relationship with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive whom US intelligence agencies believe was spying for China. Reports then surfaced of a second affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reported directly to him, and later of a third with another employee.CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO, and former Synopsys CEO Harvey Jones has become Nvidia’s first-ever board chair. Huang has been asked to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month.The campaign’s site sums up its ask in one line: “Thirty-three years deserve an answer.” The board’s first chance to give one comes next week, when Nvidia reports earnings on November 17 and Kress addresses employees at an all-hands meeting the following morning.Your child uses AI every day.
